Pakistan vs China vs Bangladesh vs Vietnam vs India: Where Should You Manufacture in 2026?

✎ FABRIOZA Team 📅 August 1, 2026 🔄 Updated: August 1, 2026 ☕ 9 min read
Home › Blog › 5-Country Matrix
TL;DR: Under ~500 pieces per style: Pakistan (50-piece MOQs, 20-piece trials, knits/sportswear). Volume basics at 5,000+: Bangladesh. Technical outerwear programs: Vietnam. Widest fabric variety and artisan wovens: India. Fastest everything with every category under one roof — at 500+ MOQs and rising costs: China. The full matrix and decision rules below.

Every "best country for manufacturing" article is written by a factory in that country — including this one, and we say so upfront: we are a Sialkot factory. What makes this page different is that the matrix below tells you when not to choose Pakistan, with the same numbers we use to advise our own clients.

Decision Rules by Order Size

  • 20–100 pieces per style: Pakistan is realistically your only factory-direct option among the five — the others start at 300+. (Domestic US/EU studios also serve this range at 2–4× the unit price.)
  • 100–1,000 pieces: Pakistan for knits/sportswear/streetwear; India if the line is woven dresses or print-heavy fashion; China if you need complex synthetics or mixed categories in one shipment.
  • 1,000–5,000 pieces: quote Pakistan, India and China against each other on landed cost — the winner varies by product.
  • 5,000+ of basics: Bangladesh, full stop. Technical outerwear at volume: Vietnam.

What "Landed Cost" Changes

FOB price comparisons mislead. Add duty and freight and the picture moves: for EU brands, Pakistan's GSP+ and Bangladesh's EBA (both worth roughly 9–12% vs paying full duty) often beat a cheaper Chinese FOB price; for US brands, China's Section 301 exposure does the same in reverse. Always compare DDP-to-your-door quotes — our costs guide walks the math.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best country to manufacture clothing for a startup?

Pakistan, in most cases - it is the only major exporter where 50-piece MOQs are standard and 20-piece trial runs exist, so a startup can test real production without 300-1,000-piece commitments. Domestic US/EU studios serve the same range at roughly 2-4x the unit price.

What is the cheapest country to manufacture clothing?

At high volume, Bangladesh - its giant factories produce basics at the world's lowest per-unit prices, with MOQs of 1,000-3,000 pieces. Below ~500 pieces, Pakistan is usually cheapest in practice because factories will actually take the order without surcharges.

Is China still worth it for clothing manufacturing in 2026?

Yes for complex synthetics, mixed-category orders and speed - China's supply chain remains unmatched in breadth. The trade-offs are 300-500+ MOQs, rising labor costs and US Section 301 tariff exposure that can erase the FOB advantage for American brands.

Which country is best for sportswear and team uniforms?

Pakistan - specifically the Sialkot cluster, the world's sports-goods manufacturing hub, with deep sublimation and decoration capability at 15-50-piece MOQs. Vietnam leads for tier-1 technical activewear programs at 1,000+ volumes.

Should I compare factories on FOB or landed cost?

Landed cost (DDP), always. Duty preferences (Pakistan/Bangladesh into the EU) and tariff penalties (China into the US) routinely swing totals by 10-25%, more than the FOB gap between countries.
